key_insight: A measurement-free protocol uses coherent control of three superconducting cavities to correct photon loss and extend logical-qubit lifetime beyond an unprotected encoding.
engineering_relevance: Correcting dominant photon-loss errors locally could reduce the burden on an outer quantum error-correcting code in superconducting hardware.
method: Encode a logical qubit in one cavity using the lowest-order binomial code.
Use two ancillary cavities and Josephson-junction-based nonlinear couplings for coherent, measurement-free correction.
Optimize the waiting time between successive correction rounds.
evidence_signal: Numerical simulations with experimentally realistic parameters report 99% single-photon-loss correction fidelity and a 1.2–1.8× logical-lifetime extension over unprotected {|0⟩, |1⟩} Fock encoding.
watch_item: The reported gains are simulation-based; experimental validation must establish whether hardware imperfections preserve the modest lifetime advantage.
paper_title: A measurement-free quantum error correction protocol for superconducting cavities
